description: FireABM is a spatial agent-based evacuation model published with a demonstration notebook and experiment code. The CyberGIS README describes vehicles representing households on a road network, three routing strategies and a spreading wildfire that can close roads and force rerouting. Users provide road and hazard settings and run the notebook or larger experiments; outputs are simulated evacuation routes, times and comparative strategy results. Geography follows the road network supplied to the model; the repository also documents HPC execution for larger runs. GitHub metadata states Apache-2.0 licensing. A limitation is that the available workflow reproduces research experiments but does not establish that each household decision or wildfire progression matches an observed emergency. HPC requirements may matter for large scenarios. The model can test road closures and evacuation routing for emergency planning. It is distinct from a general traffic simulator because it represents evolving wildfire access constraints. No notebook, map or simulation result was downloaded. The related catalogue record model-sumo supplies a general road-traffic simulator; this agent model focuses on wildfire closure and household evacuation, with no direct interface established.
inputs: Road network, household agents, wildfire spread and routing strategy
name: FireABM evacuation routing model
